name: PHP Nov release
tile_line: 17 advisories; criticals need non-default or rare setups.
tldr: PHP's 19 Nov 2026 releases fix 17 advisories, 7 critical. Each critical one needs a non-default setting or an uncommon setup, and none is reported exploited. One update to the 19 Nov releases fixes all of them; restart PHP workers after.
summary: The 17 advisories are 7 critical, 4 high and 6 medium, plus a bundled uriparser update (CVE-2026-48841), which is why some count 18. Four have public lab or test exploits. Two others close gaps in October's exploited [PHP2Shell](/php2shell/) fix.

affected.label: PHP older than the 19 Nov 2026 fix
affected.text: PHP 8.2 to 8.5 below 8.5.13, 8.4.28, 8.3.37 or 8.2.36. PHP 8.6.0 (19 Nov) is fixed. Some bugs only hit 8.3 and later, or only 8.5: see each one. 8.1 and older get no fixes from PHP. Distros may backport fixes without changing the version number.

affected.label: You use an affected feature
affected.text: Each critical bug needs a specific setting or setup, listed under The bugs above. The main ones: sessions stored in files with upload progress on (phpAfterShell, session serializer mismatch); a web server that reuses its connections to PHP-FPM (request smuggling); a non-thread-safe build logging startup warnings to a file (timezone cache); and PHP 8.5 with fatal error backtraces on (two bugs). Most need workers that serve many requests, which PHP-FPM and mod_php do.

do.label: Update PHP and restart
do.text: Update to 8.6.0, 8.5.13, 8.4.28, 8.3.37 or 8.2.36 (19 Nov 2026), then restart every PHP worker. This fixes all 17 advisories.

do.label: Check the critical ones first
do.text: [phpAfterShell](/phpaftershell/), [PHP-FPM request smuggling](/php-fpm-smuggling/) and [PHP session RCE](/php-sessions/) each have a full page with checks. The other four critical bugs and the highs are explained under The bugs above.

do.label: Can't update yet? Stopgaps
do.text: Turn off session upload progress (`session.upload_progress.enabled = 0`) and FastCGI connection reuse in your web server. On PHP 8.5, set `fatal_error_backtraces = 0`, or at least keep `zend.exception_ignore_args = On` as in `php.ini-production`. These remove some attack paths, not the bugs.

bugs.title: phpAfterShell: half-written session files
bugs.text: PHP's default file session storage can mix an old and a new session when a write is cut short, letting an attacker inject objects. Also needs attacker data in the session, a worker killed mid-write and a usable gadget chain in the app.

bugs.title: PHP-FPM request smuggling
bugs.text: An attacker with no login can hide a second request in one web request and run PHP code, but only where the web server reuses its connections to PHP-FPM (off by default in nginx and Apache) and the app leaves part of the request body unread.

bugs.title: Session serializer mismatch
bugs.text: Upload progress can let an attacker with no login run code, but only where sessions are written with one serializer and read with another, and the app has a usable gadget chain.

bugs.title: Timezone cache use-after-free
bugs.text: Every branch. Needs a non-thread-safe build (PHP-FPM, Apache mod_php or CGI) whose `error_log` writes to a file, a startup warning written there (for example an invalid `date.timezone`), and a request to a fresh worker. A request with no login can crash it. A public lab exploit runs code, but reads the worker's memory addresses from inside the lab; PHP calls a remote bypass of that "plausible", not shown.

bugs.title: Use-after-free in magic method backtraces
bugs.text: PHP 8.5 only, with `fatal_error_backtraces` on (the 8.5 default) and `zend.exception_ignore_args` off. That's the built-in default, but `php.ini-production` turns it on, which blocks this. The app must pass attacker-sized data into a `__call()` or `__callStatic()` method so a memory or time limit hits at the right moment, and the attacker needs known memory addresses. PHP confirmed code execution in testing; no code is public.

bugs.title: Use-after-free after interrupted session cleanup
bugs.text: PHP 8.3 to 8.5 workers that serve many requests (PHP-FPM or mod_php), with an app callback that runs during session cleanup and that an attacker can make hit a fatal error. A later request on the same worker can then reuse freed memory. One of two gaps PHP found in the October [PHP2Shell](/php2shell/) fix; PHP says code execution hasn't been demonstrated.

bugs.title: Fatal-error backtrace refilled after shutdown
bugs.text: PHP 8.5 only. Needs per-directory settings that change `max_memory_limit` or zlib output compression, and a later request on the same worker that produces an early warning. The second gap in the October PHP2Shell fix. PHP says code execution hasn't been demonstrated. Workaround: `fatal_error_backtraces = 0`.

bugs.title: PHP-FPM worker to master privileges
bugs.text: Someone who can already run PHP code in an FPM worker can run commands with the FPM master's privileges, which are commonly root, when `catch_workers_output` is on. Matters most on shared hosting.

bugs.title: HTTPS URLs with an uppercase S sent unencrypted
bugs.text: PHP's stream functions such as `file_get_contents()` sent `HTTPS://`, `httpS://` or `FTPS://` URLs without TLS, redirects included, so someone watching the network can read passwords, tokens or uploads.

bugs.title: Folded response headers burn CPU
bugs.text: A server PHP fetches from can send folded HTTP response headers that tie up the CPU.

bugs.title: Signed Phar accepted with a plain hash
bugs.text: Someone who can replace an OpenSSL-signed Phar archive, but not its `.pubkey` file, can swap the signature for a plain hash and still have it accepted.
